clue.text: Writer having revised Part One spies wasted worker at forge

indicators.note: something revised has been reworked, so these letters are put into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the CIA is the American spy agency
wasted is slang for intoxicated, as is high
a smith works metal at a forge

explanation.surface: An author reworks the first part of a novel about spies and a drunken blacksmith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' turns PART plus I into PATRI; the rest is a charade of synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist wrote Strangers on a Train and the Ripley thrillers, so she is a writer.

clue.text: Defence starts to address legal issues behind injunction

indicators.note: the starts of the following five words are taken, one letter from each

explanation.surface: A lawyer's defence begins by tackling legal points raised by a court order.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea that one was elsewhere when the crime happened is a classic legal defence.

clue.text: Protest about WW1 battle charge after start of truce

indicators.note: charge comes after the truce letter, so its synonym follows it

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Mons in Belgium was the site of the first British battle of the First World War

indicators.note: the start of the word truce is its first letter

parts.note: a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a WW1 battle charge made just after a truce began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks military beside 'battle', but it means a price.
explanation.definitionFit: To remonstrate is to object forcefully, a synonym of the verb protest.

clue.text: For trophy unfairly taken, Celtic exploited hole in formation?

indicators.note: exploited suggests the letters are used and worked over, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Celtic took advantage of a gap in the opposition's defensive formation to win a trophy unfairly.
explanation.walkthrough: The football surface hides a 2015 story: a famous Zimbabwean animal shot by a trophy hunter. 'formation?' hints at the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zimbabwean big cat was lured out of a reserve and killed by a trophy hunter, a killing widely condemned as unfair.

clue.text: Styled on wife-beating it becomes work of remorse and conscience

indicators.note: letters styled are fashioned anew, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tract against domestic violence becomes a study in guilt and conscience.
explanation.walkthrough: The Middle English title means 'again-bite of in-wit', remorse of conscience; Joyce quotes it in Ulysses.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourteenth-century devotional book's title literally means the prick of conscience, so it is a work about remorse.

clue.text: Transaction to import books concerning London's Hampstead Heath?

indicators.note: to import is to bring something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a deal is a business transaction
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A property deal is struck to bring books to a London beauty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Hampstead Heath is a London park, and in Cockney rhyming slang 'Hampstead Heath' means teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to teeth, which the rhyming slang phrase stands for.

clue.text: Actor put in frock that's lifted without notice?

indicators.note: without means the notice letters are left out
in a down entry, lifted means read upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: to be ordained is to be made a priest, i.e. put in clerical frock
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: An actor dressed in a frock that is whipped up without warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's lifted' turns ORDAINED into DENIADRO; 'without' removes AD from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert, star of Taxi Driver and Raging Bull, is a celebrated screen actor.

clue.text: Fortune to keep after taxes

indicators.note: the words Fortune to keep the answer held inside them, across the gap

explanation.surface: A fortune you get to keep once the tax man has taken his share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fortune to keep' reads as a phrase about wealth, but 'Fortune to' holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Net pay or profit is what remains once deductions such as tax are made.

clue.text: See 23
Fat old woman gets cold burger

parts.note: big can mean fat or large
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: An overweight older woman picks up a burger that has gone cold.
explanation.definitionFit: McDonald's best-known double-decker sandwich is a beef burger.

clue.text: Would he calculate mc2 of E in beer mug?

parts.note: a stein is a large earthenware beer mug, German in origin

explanation.surface: A puzzle about who would work out the energy formula for E sitting in a beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: E = mc² is the formula linking energy to mass; the clue's E is both part of the formula and letters taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist is famous for the equation that equates energy with mass times the speed of light squared.

clue.text: See 4
Confusing passages, Bryn Terfel finally has it sorted

indicators.note: sorted means put in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Bryn and has it are taken as written, with the final letter of the singer surname Terfel between them

explanation.surface: The Welsh bass-baritone Bryn Terfel at last masters some tricky musical passages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confusing' looks like an anagram signal, but it belongs to the definition; 'sorted' does that job.
explanation.definitionFit: Mazes are networks of bewildering paths, so they are passages designed to confuse.

clue.text: Nurse at work after dark has good drink

parts.note: night is the time after dark
in can mean at one's post or at work, as in 'is she in today?'
ale is a drink of beer

explanation.surface: A nurse working a night shift enjoys a good drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Florence, the Lady with the Lamp, is the most famous nurse in British history.

clue.text: Very intense compilers keen to neck wallop

indicators.note: to neck is to swallow, so the wallop goes down inside the other piece

parts.note: the setters writing as a group would call themselves we
a wallop is a hit
hot can mean keen or eager, as in hot on something

explanation.surface: Puzzle setters eager to down some strong beer.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallop is also British slang for beer, which suits the drinking surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal glowing white is hotter than red, so the word figuratively means extremely intense or passionate.

clue.text: See 1
Dismal or dark horse

definitions.meaning: dismal weather or a dismal mood is gloomy and dull
a dark, overcast sky looks dull and colourless
a horse with a white or whitish coat is called by this colour name

explanation.surface: A gloomy outlook, or a dark horse in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word means gloomy, overcast, and also names a pale-coated horse.

clue.text: Apparently carnivorous French dad to pass through!

indicators.note: apparently signals that the carnivorous dad is pictured literally, with flesh inside him

parts.note: père is French for father
something carnivorous is full of flesh, so meat is the filling

explanation.surface: A French father who seems to be a meat-eater is just passing through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' tells you to read 'carnivorous' literally: a meat-eater has his food inside him.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread throughout or penetrate something is a synonym of the verb meaning go through.

clue.text: Metal god finds Indian city

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver, a metal
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: A metal idol turns up in an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The city in Uttar Pradesh is home to the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Greek plays, others in Old English, I start to adapt

indicators.note: in places the others inside the Old English abbreviation

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: the start of adapt is its first letter

explanation.surface: A translator renders Greek drama into Old English and begins adapting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeschylus's trilogy about the house of Atreus is a set of three Greek tragedies.

clue.text: Sent aloft to assassinate but stopped by Mr Hunter

indicators.note: stopped by means the title is plugged into the middle
in a down entry, sent aloft means written upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to do in is to kill

explanation.surface: A rocket sent up to kill someone is foiled by a man called Hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent aloft' turns DO IN into NIOD, which MR then fills.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this king is called a mighty hunter before the Lord.

clue.text: Self-denial exists among cats at play with mice

indicators.note: among places one piece in the middle of another
at play suggests letters frisking about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: is means exists

explanation.surface: Self-restraint survives even where cats play with mice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at play' signals the anagram of the two animals, giving ASCETICM; 'among' then sets the 'exists' synonym into it before the final M.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere renunciation of comforts and pleasures is the practice of denying oneself.

clue.text: Brown back and midsection in Pietà or other work

indicators.note: back means the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour

indicators.note: the midsection of the five-letter word is its central letter

explanation.surface: Restorers look at the brown back and middle of Michelangelo's Pietà and other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An artwork depicting an unclothed figure is called by this term, as in a painted study.

clue.text: Rage in The Iliad confused poet

indicators.note: the letters are muddled up into a new order

explanation.surface: Achilles' rage in Homer's epic baffled a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram spans 23 and 8, with 8 holding the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine author of the Divine Comedy is one of Italy's greatest poets.

clue.text: Pull out having contest no side wins

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with a hat
a draw is a game that ends with no winner

explanation.surface: A team retreats from a match where nobody wins.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat or retire from something is a synonym of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Husband and uncle eviscerated in shade

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies

indicators.note: eviscerated means gutted, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A husband and an uncle are gutted, hiding in the shadows.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour or tint is a shade, as in a different shade of blue.

clue.text: Old move on — relative takes in V&A

indicators.note: takes in means one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: an aunt is a relative
the V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

explanation.surface: Time to go: a relative is visiting the V&A museum.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic exclamation means begone or go away, an old way to tell someone to move on.

clue.text: Clever Kate Minola departs

parts.note: Katherina Minola is the shrew of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew
D is the abbreviation for departs in timetables

explanation.surface: A clever Shakespeare heroine walks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Being astute and sharp-witted is a synonym of clever.

clue.text: French head drinking English wine looked wobbly

indicators.note: drinking means taking the other piece inside

parts.note: tête is French for head
red is wine

explanation.surface: A Frenchman downs English wine and starts to sway.
explanation.definitionFit: To wobble unsteadily as if about to fall is to sway in this way.
